subject: sea bream
title: Wild Fish Learned to Tell Two Divers Apart, Not by Their Faces

scenes.text: Wild fish learned to follow one diver and ignore another.
Eight metres down in the Mediterranean, a scientist fed sea bream only after they followed her fifty metres.
In twelve days, about twenty wild fish were tagging along behind her.
Then a second diver swam the other way. By day two, most fish chose her, not him.
How? Masks hide faces underwater. The fish read small colour patches on their wetsuits and fins.
When both divers wore identical gear, the fish were lost. To a fish, you are your outfit.

description:
In a 2025 Biology Letters study, Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior researchers trained wild sea bream at a Mediterranean site 8 metres deep to follow a diver 50 metres for food.
The fish learned to pick the rewarding diver over a second one, most likely by colour patches on their gear, and could not tell them apart when both wore identical gear.
Would you dive with fish that know you?
first_comment: The fish were volunteers: free to come and go. The scientists even saw them swim up and inspect divers' hands and hair. Next test: faces?
